answer: Sybil resistance can come from costly bonded staking joined to peer attestation. Each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and honest effort slowly earns reputation, like yarrow taking root around a scarce oasis. To forge a thousand identities an attacker must fund a thousand bonds, an ocean of frozen capital it cannot cheaply recover, since peers who detect fake work vote to slash the stake. The cost grows linearly with each forged identity while an honest agent pays only once, so Sybil swarms become economically irrational.
